statusModifiers.riskEmphasis: Higher risk of neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, mucositis, dose delay or reduction.
statusModifiers.actions:
Energy and protein
• Energy 30–35 kcal/kg/day; protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day
• Protein options (aim 20–25 g per meal): 2 eggs, or 100 g paneer or tofu, or 1 cup dal + curd, or 1 glass milk + 30 g nuts, or 30 g soy chunks, or fish/chicken if eaten
Symptom-wise management
• Mucositis: Incorporate soft, moist, non-acidic, non-spicy foods. Options: khichdi with ghee, curd rice, egg custard, mashed banana, ragi porridge, dal soup, idli soaked in sambar, smoothies. Serve at room temperature or cool; salt-soda rinse before meals
• Neuropathy: Include B-vitamin foods daily. Options: B1/B6: oats, ragi, whole wheat, dals, groundnuts, sunflower seeds; B12: eggs, milk, curd, paneer (fish if eaten); folate: spinach, methi, rajma, chana. No alcohol
• Taste change/fatigue: Include cold protein foods. Options: curd, paneer cubes, boiled egg, chilled lassi, chana salad, fruit-curd bowl; use herbs (mint, coriander, jeera) in place of lemon marinades
• Neutropenia: freshly cooked food, washed and peeled fruit, boiled water. Avoid street food, raw sprouts, unpasteurized milk
•Steroid days: Options:ragi, jowar, bajra, oats, barley, whole dals, chana.
Moderate sodium:flavour with ginger, jeera, herbs, lemon; limit pickle, papad, namkeen
•Nausea:Include small bland meals.Options:plain idli, toast, khakhra, poha, ginger tea
Red-flag notes
• Fever of 100°F (37.8°C) or above, chills or feeling unwell (possible neutropenia/febrile neutropenia): consult your oncologist immediately for treatment
• Unable to eat, drink or swallow due to mouth sores, or vomiting that stops fluids staying down: inform your oncologist the same day

• Cardiac risk: heart-healthy fats. Options: almonds, walnuts, flaxseed, chia, mustard or groundnut oil, fish if eaten. Moderate sodium (flavour with herbs, jeera, ginger). No high-dose antioxidant supplements

Symptom-wise management
• Add the symptom measures of the accompanying chemotherapy class
• Infusion day: light meal before the infusion. Options: idli, poha, toast with egg, upma, khichdi, banana. Avoid a heavy meal that may worsen nausea
• First doses (tumor lysis prevention): fluids as directed by the oncologist (about 2.5–3 L/day unless restricted). Options: water, coconut water, buttermilk, ORS. Individualized by renal function and fluid input/output

Red-flag notes
• Fever of 100°F (37.8°C) or above, chills or feeling unwell (possible neutropenia/febrile neutropenia): consult your oncologist immediately for treatment, including weeks to months after the last dose
• Fever, chills, breathlessness, rash or swelling of lips or face during an infusion: tell the nursing staff and oncologist immediately
• Reduced urine, muscle cramps or confusion after first doses: consult your oncologist immediately

statusModifiers.riskEmphasis: Higher risk of weight loss, dehydration with colitis, and steroid complications.
statusModifiers.actions:
Energy and protein
• Energy 30–35 kcal/kg/day; protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day
• Protein options: eggs, paneer, curd, dal, tofu, milk, soy chunks, fish/chicken if eaten
Symptom-wise management
• Diarrhea/colitis: ORS (sachet, coconut water, salted buttermilk, rice water) and a low-residue diet. Options: rice, banana, curd rice, toast, boiled potato, stewed apple
• Hyperglycemia: low-GI carbs. Options: ragi, jowar, bajra, oats, barley, whole dals, chana
• Fatigue/dizziness: ONS, small frequent meals (banana with nut butter, curd with fruit, egg sandwich, paneer roll), salt as advised
• If steroids start: low sodium (flavour with herbs, jeera, ginger, lemon; limit pickle, papad, namkeen), low-GI carbs (ragi, jowar, oats), more protein (eggs, paneer, dal, curd), calcium foods (milk, curd, paneer, ragi, sesame), vitamin D foods (egg yolk, fortified milk, fatty fish if eaten, sun-exposed mushrooms; 15–20 min morning sunlight). No alcohol
Red-flag notes
• 4 or more stools above baseline, blood in stool, abdominal pain or diarrhea with fever: consult your oncologist immediately
• Fever of 100°F (37.8°C) or above, chills or feeling unwell (infection, especially if on steroids): consult your oncologist immediately for treatment
• Extreme thirst, frequent urination, severe fatigue, dizziness or confusion (possible high sugar or adrenal/thyroid changes): consult your oncologist immediately
• New cough, breathlessness or severe headache: consult your oncologist immediately

radiotherapy.guidance:
Energy and protein
• Energy: 25–30 kcal/kg/day; protein: 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day, individualised to clinical requirements.
• Small, frequent, energy- and protein-dense meals; fortify foods with milk powder, curd, paneer, nut paste or suitable oils.
• Protein options: eggs, paneer, curd, dal, tofu, milk, soy chunks, fish/chicken if eaten.
Fibre, prebiotics and probiotics
• Include tolerated fibre sources such as oats, banana, cooked vegetables and whole grains when bowel function permits.
• During significant diarrhoea, temporarily reduce insoluble fibre; increase fibre gradually for constipation if appropriate.
• Prebiotic foods: oats, banana and tolerated vegetables; reduce fermentable foods if bloating or diarrhoea worsens.
• Pasteurised curd/yoghurt may be included if tolerated. Avoid routine probiotic supplements in severely immunocompromised patients unless approved by the treating team.
Symptom-wise nutritional management
• Mucositis/oral ulcers: Soft, moist, non-spicy and non-acidic foods; avoid coarse, sharp-textured and very hot foods. Maintain oral hygiene and adequate fluid intake.
• Dysphagia/painful swallowing: Modify texture and fluid consistency according to swallowing safety; arrange assessment if swallowing difficulty develops.
• Dermatitis: Maintain adequate protein, energy, fluids and micronutrients to support tissue maintenance. Follow the oncology team's skin-care instructions.
• Nausea/vomiting: Include Small, frequent meals; bland, easily tolerated foods; avoid strong food odours and greasy foods if they worsen symptoms.
• Diarrhoea/radiation enteritis: Temporarily reduce insoluble fibre; adjust lactose and fermentable foods according to tolerance. Replace fluid and electrolyte losses as indicated; use ORS when appropriate.
• Constipation: Adequate fluids, tolerated fibre and activity as clinically appropriate.
• Bloating/abdominal discomfort: Smaller meals; adjust individual triggers, lactose or fermentable foods if they worsen symptoms.
• Dry mouth/taste changes: Moist foods, gravies and tolerated fluids; adjust flavours and food temperatures according to preference.
• Fatigue/poor appetite: 5–6 small meals/snacks, food fortification and nourishing fluids or ONS as required.
Micronutrients and hydration
• Ensure dietary adequacy of iron, folate, vitamin B12, vitamin D, calcium, zinc and other micronutrients according to assessment; supplement documented deficiencies as indicated.
• Avoid unnecessary high-dose antioxidant or micronutrient supplements without clinical review.
• Monitor hydration and replace gastrointestinal losses according to clinical need.
Monitoring and red-flag notes
• Monitor weight, food intake, hydration, bowel habits and functional status closely.
• If intake remains inadequate despite counselling, fortification and ONS, assess promptly for enteral nutrition.
• Persistent vomiting, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, significant swallowing difficulty or severe skin breakdown: urgent clinical assessment.
• Fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or above during cancer treatment: contact the oncology team immediately and follow its emergency instructions.

radiotherapy.guidance:
Energy and protein
• Energy: 25–30 kcal/kg/day; protein: 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day, individualised to clinical requirements.
• Provide regular meals and 2–3 snacks; fortify foods and add ONS if intake is insufficient.
• Protein options: eggs, paneer, curd, dal, tofu, milk, soy chunks, fish/chicken if eaten.
Fibre, prebiotics and probiotics
• Include tolerated fibre from oats, fruits, vegetables, whole grains and legumes when bowel function permits.
• Reduce insoluble fibre temporarily during significant diarrhoea; increase fibre gradually for constipation when appropriate.
• Include prebiotic foods such as oats, banana and tolerated vegetables; modify fermentable foods if bloating occurs.
• Pasteurised curd/yoghurt may be included if tolerated. Probiotic supplements require clinical approval, particularly during immunosuppression.
Symptom-wise nutritional management
• Mucositis/oral ulcers: Incorporate Soft, moist, non-irritating foods; avoid spicy, acidic and coarse foods when painful.
• Dysphagia: Modify food texture and fluid consistency according to swallowing safety; seek assessment if needed.
• Dermatitis: Maintain adequate nutrition and follow prescribed skin-care measures.
• Nausea/vomiting: Small, frequent meals and fluids; avoid individual food triggers.
• Diarrhoea: Adjust insoluble fibre, lactose and fermentable foods according to tolerance; replace fluid and electrolyte losses as indicated.
• Constipation: Encourage suitable fluids, tolerated fibre and activity.
• Bloating/abdominal discomfort: Smaller meals and adjustment of individual food triggers.
• Dry mouth/taste changes: Moist foods, gravies and tolerated flavour adjustments.
• Fatigue/poor appetite: Nutrient-dense snacks, food fortification and ONS if required.
Micronutrients and hydration
• Ensure adequate dietary vitamins and minerals; correct documented deficiencies and avoid unnecessary high-dose supplementation.
• Maintain adequate fluid intake and replace gastrointestinal losses as clinically indicated.
Monitoring and red-flag notes
• Monitor weight, appetite, intake and treatment-related symptoms; intensify support if weight loss continues.
• Persistent vomiting, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, significant swallowing difficulty or severe skin reactions: prompt medical assessment.
• Fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or above during cancer treatment: contact the oncology team immediately and follow its emergency instructions.

radiotherapy.guidance:
Energy and protein
• Energy: approximately 25–30 kcal/kg/day; protein: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day, individualised to clinical requirements.
• Maintain balanced meals with adequate protein and energy.
• Protein options: eggs, paneer, curd, dal, tofu, milk, soy chunks, fish/chicken if eaten.
Fibre, prebiotics and probiotics
• Include a variety of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, oats and legumes as tolerated.
• Adjust fibre according to bowel symptoms and radiation site; reduce insoluble fibre temporarily during significant diarrhoea.
• Include tolerated prebiotic foods such as oats, banana and vegetables.
• Pasteurised curd/yoghurt may be consumed if tolerated; probiotic supplements are not routinely required to prevent radiation toxicity.
Symptom-wise nutritional management
• Mucositis/oral ulcers: Soft, moist foods; avoid spicy, acidic, coarse and very hot foods if irritating.
• Dysphagia: Modify food texture and fluid consistency according to swallowing safety.
• Dermatitis: Maintain balanced nutrition, adequate protein and fluids; follow the oncology team's skin-care guidance.
• Nausea/vomiting: Small, frequent meals and fluids as tolerated.
• Diarrhoea: Adjust fibre and lactose according to tolerance; replace fluid and electrolyte losses as indicated.
• Constipation: Adequate fluids, appropriate fibre and activity when clinically suitable.
• Bloating/abdominal discomfort: Identify and adjust individual food triggers.
• Dry mouth/taste changes: Moist foods, gravies and tolerated flavour adjustments.
• Fatigue/poor appetite: Maintain regular meals and add nutrient-dense snacks if intake declines.
Micronutrients and hydration
• Maintain micronutrient adequacy through a balanced diet; supplement only when clinically indicated.
• Maintain adequate hydration according to clinical requirements.
Monitoring and red-flag notes
• Monitor weight, appetite, dietary intake and symptoms to detect nutritional deterioration early.
• Persistent vomiting, severe diarrhoea, dehydration, significant swallowing difficulty or severe skin reactions: prompt medical assessment.
• Fever of 38°C (100.4°F) or above during cancer treatment: contact the oncology team immediately and follow its emergency instructions.
